# eia-860m

**EIA's monthly inventory of US power plants (EIA-860M), for the infrastructure layers**

- **Version recorded:** 2026-08
- **Categories:** `emcomm`, `navigation-maps`
- **Upstream:** <https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/>

## What it does

Installs one file, EIA-860M's monthly generator workbook (about 14 MB), under /usr/local/share/hammunition/data/eia-860m/. Nothing reads it on its own: `hammunition maps infra import --from-eia` turns the operating plants in your map regions into a layer for QMapShack, Navit, phones and the browser map, one point a plant with its operator, technologies, nameplate megawatts and generator count, named "Power plants (EIA-860M <month>)".

## Why you would want it

Where the grid's generation is, and how big each plant is, matters when the grid is down: which towns sit near a hydro or a peaker, where a plant's own staff and fuel are. OpenStreetMap's `power` layer places more plants (Vermont's rooftop solar arrays among them) but rarely carries capacity, fuel or status; EIA's carries all three for every plant of 1 MW or more.

## Before it will work

Map regions installed (`hammunition install osm-regions`): the import keeps what lies in their boxes. QMapShack, Navit or the browser map to see the layer.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install eia-860m --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- data (Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration (Aug 2026), public domain, https://www.eia.gov/about/copyrights_reuse.php): https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/august_generator2026.xlsx (13,955,142 bytes)

## Known problems

US only (`wri-power-plants` covers other countries). Plants under 1 MW are not in EIA-860M. The workbook's address changes the month after it is published, so an install from EIA fails after that until the pin is regenerated or moved, unless a LAN mirror holds the pinned copy. The import reads the workbook's 56 MB operating sheet row by row; it takes a few seconds.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: reinstall
- A new month about the fourth week of the next. The weekly pin review runs `scripts/gen_eia860m_pin.py --check`, which goes red when a newer month is out or the pinned month has moved to EIA's archive; `scripts/gen_eia860m_pin.py` pins the newest month (a 14 MB download) and `--follow-move` keeps the pinned month at its archive address after checking the archive's copy has the pinned digest.

## Where to get help with the software itself

EIA's electricity data team, through the contact on https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/; Hammunition only converts the workbook.
